newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: France promises fair screening for Thomson - S.Korea.
newsitem.headline: France promises fair screening for Thomson - S.Korea.

text.p: South Korea's Finance Ministry said on Monday a visiting French envoy promised fair competition for the re-launched privatisation of state-run Thomson SA.

French presidential envoy Jean-Claude Paye met Korean Finance Minister Han Seung-soo to explain why Paris scuttled the sale of Thomson Multimedia to South Korea's Daewoo Electronics, a move that sparked anger in Seoul.
A Finance Ministry statement quoted Paye as saying the government's decision was regrettable.

But he said Paris had to scrap the sale of Thomson SA to Lagardere Groupe in December after objections by the French privatisation commission to plans to spin off the consumer electronics unit to Daewoo.
"For whoever emerges as a new candidate for the privatisation, fair screening will be made," a statement from the Finance Ministry quoted Paye as saying.
Han said a Daewoo purchase of Thomson Multimedia would have contributed to better economic relations between France and South Korea.
"If the privatisation had been successful, that would have greatly helped Korea-French economic ties," Han said.
South Korean industry leaders slammed the decision as racist and unfair and hinted there could be repercussions for French business in the booming Asian economy.
Han said he hoped the procedure for the re-launched privatisation would be transparent.
It was unclear if Daewoo, which would have become the biggest television set maker in the world with the acquisition of Thomson Multimedia, was still interested in the company.
Daewoo officials were not available for comment late on Monday.

Just one week after scrapping its original plan, the French government said it would privatise Thomson in two halves -- selling its profitable defence arm Thomson-CSF first and then the money-losing consumer electronics division.
